decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “I can add a link.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by entering a link conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, delete ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client only confirms “I can ... edit it,” without identifying editable fields.
decisions.note: Prototype review: generic editing is recorded, but the transcript does not establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add, edit, delete ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client: “I can ... delete it.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: bookmark deletion conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “tag filters”; Round 1 client confirms “I can ... tag them.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning tags is explicitly confirmed.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Collections and tag filters.” Round 1 client says the basics, including tags, are working.
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting tags as filters conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search with `⌘/Ctrl + K`.” Round 1 client: “I can ... search”; Round 2 client: “find them with search.” No response identifies searchable fields, case handling, #tag syntax, Boolean/group syntax, or quoted phrases.
decisions.note: Prototype and final implementation review: generic search is confirmed, but its reference-defined scope and semantics cannot be established from the transcript.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “Sorting”; the client accepts the basic application while requesting unrelated changes.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the recorded ability to sort conforms to the reference's sort-key requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client reports the presented app behavior: “I had to type in the title and the little description myself,” then supplies the expected replacement: “when I paste in a link, I want the app to go grab the page's name and summary (and its little icon) ... automatically.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: manual metadata entry diverged from automatic collection; the client identified the mismatch and requested automatic collection.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “favorite bookmarks.” Round 1 client distinguishes the missing requirement: “I'd expected a way to mark a link as ‘read it later’ ... The star/favorite ... isn't quite the same,” and asks for it.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client requested the missing unread/read-later state as a distinct feature rather than accepting favorites as a substitute.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client requests “see just those in one place — a to-read pile” and explicitly asks for “a read-later view.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the client surfaced and requested the missing dedicated unread-bookmark view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client specifies “a to-read pile that empties as I get through it.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: this expresses the missing behavior of marking an item read so it leaves the unread view.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its title, description, and favicon,” omitting the required preview image. Round 2 client praises title/description autofill and gives final approval but does not identify or accept the missing preview-image behavior.
decisions.note: Implementation review: the revised metadata decision still diverges because REF-BM-02 also requires a preview image. The client's approval is not an explicit statement of that difference, so it is not an accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Fields remain editable”; Round 1 already presented general bookmark editing, and Round 2 client confirms the completed autofill flow.
decisions.note: Implementation review: collected fields remain editable in the save flow and the application retains post-save editing, conforming to before/after editability.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Added a dedicated Read later view with a live count.” Round 2 client confirms the pile is “right there in the sidebar with its count.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: the revised dedicated unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Bookmarks can enter the queue while saving or from any bookmark card.” Round 2 client confirms “I can drop things into it while saving or from a card.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: bookmarks can be marked for later, conforming to the unread-state requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “‘Mark as read’ immediately removes an item from the queue.” Round 2 client confirms “marking one as read clears it out of the queue.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: marking a bookmark read removes it from the unread list, conforming to the reference.
